title: Comparative analytical writing
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches how to write a single comparative thesis, while the new point teaches the point-by-point structure of a comparative essay, so they are related but not the same idea.

draft.title: Comparative analytical writing
card: A comparative essay discusses two texts together. It shows how each text handles the same idea, and where they are alike or different.
each paragraph takes one point, such as how the texts treat hope, and discusses both texts in turn. This keeps the comparison in view.
words such as similarly, whereas and in contrast show the reader how the two texts relate.
each text needs its own evidence and analysis in the paragraph. Naming a technique and its effect for both texts makes the comparison fair.
draft.remember: Compare the texts inside each paragraph, one shared point at a time.

a.q: Which plan for a comparative essay on how two stories treat loneliness is organised point by point?
opts: Each paragraph discusses both stories on one point
One paragraph for each story, then a short ending
All of story one, then all of story two
A summary of each story, then the thesis
a.why: A point-by-point essay puts both texts into every paragraph, built around one shared point. Discussing one whole text and then the other keeps the texts apart, so the comparison is left until the end.
a.clue: Where do both texts appear in the plan?

b.q: In a paragraph on how two poems treat the sea, Sam writes: 'Poem A uses a storm to show danger, whereas Poem B uses calm water to show comfort.' What makes this a comparison?
opts: It links both poems on one point with a contrast word
It names a technique used in only one poem
It describes the plot of each poem in order
It gives a personal opinion about the sea
b.why: Sam places both poems in one sentence on one shared point, the sea, and uses whereas to show the difference. Naming techniques is useful, but the comparison comes from joining the two poems on the same point.
b.clue: Look at how the two poems sit in one sentence.

a.best: Each paragraph discusses both stories on one point

b.best: It links both poems on one point with a contrast word
